scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Both user LANs lost cross-AS connectivity this morning: pc1
(195.11.14.2) cannot reach pc2 (200.1.1.2) and pc2 cannot reach
pc1. Each PC still reaches its own gateway fine. Our NOC checked
router1: its inter-AS interface eth0 shows UP and its config is
unchanged. The partner operator (AS 2) says router2's logs show
the eBGP session dropping. Find what broke.

injection.action: administratively down the inter-AS interface (eth0) on router2

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router2 eth0 (193.10.11.2/24, the inter-AS
  interface toward router1)
Mechanism: router2's eth0 is DOWN, so the physical/L2 path between
  the two ASes is broken at router2's side. router2 immediately
  loses its 193.10.11.0/24 connected route and its BGP route to
  195.11.14.0/24 (nexthop interface gone), and its side of the
  eBGP session drops. Traffic from pc1 toward 200.1.1.0/24 is
  blackholed on the inter-AS segment (nothing listens at
  193.10.11.2 any more), so pc1<->pc2 fails in both directions.
  Note: router1's eth0 still shows UP (the far side of the virtual
  link keeps carrier), and router1 may briefly keep showing the
  session as Established until its hold timer expires -- the
  definitive evidence is router2's eth0 being DOWN.
Localization: router2
Root cause: inter-AS link down at router2 (eth0 administratively
  down)
Fix: `ip link set eth0 up` on router2
scenario.fix_spec:
Bring the inter-AS link back up: on router2 run `ip link set eth0 up`. The
eBGP session re-establishes, the inter-AS prefixes are re-exchanged, and pc1
reaches pc2 normally. router1 needs no change -- it was healthy the whole time.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The inter-AS eBGP session between router1 (AS 1, 193.10.11.1) and router2
(AS 2, 193.10.11.2) collapsed because router2's eth0 interface — the physical
link connecting the two routers on the 193.10.11.0/24 transit segment — was
administratively brought down. At the kernel level, eth0 on router2 shows
flags <BROADCAST,MULTICAST> with no UP or LOWER_UP bits set, while router1's
eth0 correctly shows <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP>. The FRR interface log
on router2 records a link-down event at exactly 14:25:40, and the BGP daemon
log from that moment shows the session immediately transitioning to the Active
state as FRR lost the TCP connection to 193.10.11.1.

With eth0 down, router2 has no path to its BGP peer and cannot complete the
TCP handshake needed to re-establish the session; it cycles through Active
every ~16 seconds. As a direct consequence, router2's RIB contains only its
own directly connected LAN (200.1.1.0/24) and holds no BGP-learned route to
195.11.14.0/24, making pc2's side of the network completely unreachable from
pc1. Router1 eventually loses the session too once the 90-second hold timer
expires.

Root cause: router2's eth0 was administratively shut down (equivalent to
`ip link set eth0 down`), severing the only physical path between AS 1 and
AS 2.

Corrective fix: On router2, run `ip link set eth0 up` to restore the
interface. The eBGP session will re-establish within seconds, both routers
will exchange their network prefixes, and cross-AS reachability between pc1
(195.11.14.2) and pc2 (200.1.1.2) will be restored. To make the fix
persistent across restarts, ensure the startup configuration does not include
a `link-down` or equivalent directive for eth0.
